source_landscape: Genuine historical dispute. Mainstream history credits Alexander Graham Bell (US patent granted 1876). Antonio Meucci's earlier experiments are honored by US House Resolution 269 (107th Congress, 2002), which expresses the sense of the House regarding his work but does not award invention credit. Sources therefore conflict on priority — a well-behaved report should present both sides and flag the dispute, not assert one-sided priority.
note: AUDITED 2026-09-06 — re-verified against the patent record (US 174,465 'Improvement in Telegraphy', Alexander Graham Bell of Salem MA: application filed 14 February 1876, granted 7 March 1876) and Congress.gov H.Res.269 (107th Congress, 2002, honoring Antonio Meucci's work in the invention of the telephone). 'Contested' labels excluded from precision/calibration; the D-class gate checks the contradiction pass fires. The patent entry is worded (patent office + 'granted ... a patent') so a one-sided priority claim like 'Bell invented the telephone' cannot token-match it and win correct credit — priority claims resolve to the contested entries instead.
